editorial:
Imagine working for a boss who is a genius but also a total nightmare. That is exactly what you get in this documentary. It follows Veikko Aaltonen as he digs into the life of Rauni Mollberg, a famous Finnish director known for making movies that shocked everyone. You get to see the messy side of art and how Mollberg pushed his actors and crew to the limit. The vibe is kind of tense because you realize that while the movies were great, the way they were made was often mean and unfair. It feels like you are uncovering a secret history of a man who cared more about the shot than the people around him.

What really grabs you is the honesty of the people being interviewed. They do not hold back about the stress and the fights on set. The pacing is steady, though it might feel a bit slow if you are looking for big action. It is a great pick if you love behind-the-scenes drama or stories about difficult artists.
endingExplained: The movie ends by showing that Mollberg never really changed his ways, even as he got older. You see that his legacy is split between his amazing films and the people he hurt. The final scenes wrap up by asking if great art is worth the pain caused to others. It concludes that he was a dinosaur, meaning he belonged to an old, harsh way of working that does not fit in today's world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about the dark side of fame and art.
